fact_en:
Why does your heart pump faster in extreme heat?

Extreme heat forces your heart to pump faster to cool your body down through sweating!
fact_bis:
Nganong mopaspas ang pag-pump sa kasingkasing sa extreme heat?

Ang extreme heat mopapaspas sa kasingkasing aron mapabugnaw ang lawas pinaagi sa pagpanghupaw!
evidence: "Bato" is a stone (or kidney), never the heart — the body says "kasingkasing", as do 273 corpus bodies — so the headline reads "Fast Stone in the Heat".

fact_en: The lithosphere is Earth's rigid outer shell made of the crust and the very top of the mantle! It is broken into tectonic plates.
fact_bis: Ang lithosphere mao ang gahi nga gawas nga panit sa Kalibutan nga gilangkob sa crust ug sa kinatas-ang bahin sa mantle! Kini ang nabahin sa mga tectonic plate.
evidence: The card's own terms list offers "mga plate"/"mga plaka" for tectonic plates, but the title picks "plato", which a grade-5 Cebuano reader takes as a dinner plate.

fact_en: In the rock cycle, magma cooling and solidifying beneath the Earth's crust forms intrusive igneous rocks like granite!
fact_bis: Sa rock cycle, ang pagbugnaw ug pag-solidify sa magma ilawom sa crust sa Yuta nagmugna og intrusive igneous rocks sama sa granite!
evidence: Last word "Igneo" is cut off; the card itself contains "Igneous".

fact_en:
Why can you scratch gypsum with just your fingernail?

Because gypsum is a very soft mineral!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga makiskis nimo ang gypsum gamit lang ang imong kuko?

Kay kini hilabihan ka humok nga mineral!
evidence: "Lumos" means drowned/smothered in Cebuano while the body says "hilabihan ka humok", so the headline loses the card's whole point (gypsum is soft) and reads "Drowned Gypsum".

fact_en: Earthquakes are caused by the sudden movement of tectonic plates deep underground! They are not caused by severe weather conditions.
fact_bis: Ang linog tungod sa kalit nga paglihok sa tectonic plates ilawom sa yuta! Dili kini tungod sa severe weather conditions.
evidence: "Lindol Plato" is Tagalog "lindol" plus "plato" (dinner plate) where the body correctly says "linog" and "tectonic plate", so the headline names a dish rather than a plate boundary.

fact_en:
How are clouds made?

Warm ocean water evaporates into invisible water vapor, which later condenses to form the visible clouds we see in the sky!
fact_bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa mga panganod?

Ang init nga tubig sa dagat mo-evaporate ug mahimong invisible water vapor, nga unya mo-condense aron makahimo og makita nga panganod!
evidence: The body asks "Unsaon paghimo sa mga panganod?" but the title says "Pagtapak", which is stepping on/patching, so the headline reads "Stepping on the Cloud".

fact_en: Ash from an eruption usually falls downwind! This means towns on one side of a volcano may be dusty, while the other side stays clearer.
fact_bis: Kasagaran ang abo mohulog sa direksyon sa hangin! Mao nga ang mga lungsod sa usa ka kilid sa bulkan mabug-at samtang ang pikas klaro.
evidence: The body says "ang abo mohulog sa direksyon sa hangin" (ash falls downwind), but the title's "aso" is smoke — smoke does not fall and dust the towns on one side of a volcano.

fact_en:
Why does a ferry horn sound higher when it arrives and lower when it leaves?

It's a waterfront example of a moving sound source! The pitch changes as the boat moves toward or away from you.
fact_bis:
Nganong mas taas ang tunog sa busina sa ferry kung mo-abot ug mas ubos kung mo-biya?

Kini usa ka pananglitan sa naglihok nga gigikanan sa tingog sa tubig! Nag-usab ang tono kung moduol o mopayo ang sakayan.
evidence: "Buryo" is boredom/restlessness in Cebuano and occurs in no body in the corpus, while a boat horn is "busina" — the body's own word — so the headline reads "Boredom of the Ferry on the Water".

fact_en:
Is volcanic ash alive?

Nope! Volcanic ash is an earth material made of tiny rock bits. It is non-living, even when it covers plants after an eruption.
fact_bis:
Buhi ba ang volcanic ash?

Dili! Ang volcanic ash kay earth material nga gihimo sa gagmay nga bato. Dili kini buhi, bisan pa nga natabunan ang mga tanom human sa pag-erupt.
evidence: This card exists to teach that volcanic ash is tiny rock and not smoke, yet the title calls it "aso" (smoke), so the headline asserts exactly the misconception the body corrects.

fact_en:
What does the uterus look like in diagrams?

In diagrams, the uterus is the pear-shaped organ in the center, with an ovary on each side!
fact_bis:
Unsay dagway sa uterus sa mga diagram?

Sa mga diagram, ang uterus kay ang pear-shaped organ sa tunga, adunay ovary sa matag kilid!
evidence: "Pera" is money (pear is "peras", which the card's own terms carry as "hugis-peras"), so the headline promises a money-shaped uterus and drops the pear shape that is the card's only fact.

fact_en: Talking and using tools don't make us mammals! Class Mammalia is actually about shared body traits like hair, milk, and ear bones.
fact_bis: Ang pagsulti ug paggamit og tools dili maoy hinungdan nga kita mammal! Ang Class Mammalia mahitungod sa body traits sama sa hair, gatas, ug ear bones.
evidence: Last word "Mamma" is cut off; the card itself contains "Mammalia".

fact_en: A change at one level affects others! If pollution kills pond plants, the animals that eat them also disappear.
fact_bis: Ang kausaban sa usa ka level makaapekto sa uban! Kung ang pollution makapatay sa mga tanom sa lim-aw, mawala usab ang mga mananap nga mokaon kanila.
evidence: Last word "Ecosyste" is cut off; the card itself contains "Ecosystem".
